questions.stem:
Words: bird = birdo, woman = woma, house = housa, boy = boyi, happy = hap-, big = big-, old = old-, three = thri.
Which phrase follows every rule?
questions.passage:
Rules for this section:
1. An adjective comes after the noun it describes.
2. An adjective is a stem ending in a consonant (blak- = black). It takes the last vowel of its noun's root: dogo (dog) gives dogo blako.
3. Plural: add -s to the noun and to each of its adjectives.
4. After a number word (tuo = two, thri = three, fora = four), the number comes first and neither the noun nor its adjectives take -s.
5. With two adjectives, both follow the noun in the REVERSE of the English order.
6. There is no word for "the" or "a".
questions.explain: thri birdo bigo hapo ("three happy big birds") follows every rule: bird = birdo; three = thri first, no -s; happy and big take o from birdo, order reversed. woma hapa thri puts the number word after the noun instead of first (correct: thri woma hapa). thri biga housa puts the adjective before the noun, but adjectives always follow it (correct: thri housa biga). boyi bigis oldis puts -s on the adjective but not on the noun (correct: boyis bigis oldis).

1. An adjective comes after the noun it describes.
2. An adjective is a stem ending in a consonant (blak- = black). It takes the last vowel of its noun's root: dogo (dog) gives dogo blako.
3. Plural: add -s to the noun and to each of its adjectives.
4. After a number word (tuo = two, thri = three, fora = four), the number comes first and neither the noun nor its adjectives take -s.
5. With two adjectives, both follow the noun in the REVERSE of the English order.
6. There is no word for "the" or "a".
7. my, your, his, our, their are endings on the noun: -mi, -ti, -si, -mis, -sis.
8. The owner comes AFTER the thing owned and takes the ending -ve: dogo manuve = the man's dog.
9. The thing owned keeps its adjectives right after it; the owner's adjectives follow the owner.
10. Endings go on in this order: plural -s, then my/your/his/our/their, then -ve.
11. An adjective's vowel comes from its own noun's root, never from an ending.
12. Word order is subject, then object, then verb. The verb is always last.
13. The object noun takes the ending -na, added after any other ending. Its adjectives do not take -na.
14. Verb endings: -ar (present), -ir (past), -ul (future).
15. If the subject is plural (with -s, a number word, or we / they), add -en after the tense ending.
16. Negative: put nu- on the front of the verb.
17. Pronouns: mi = I, ti = you, si = he or she, mis = we, sis = they. As objects they take -na (mina = me).
18. A yes/no question puts ka at the very start of the sentence. Nothing else changes.
questions.explain: manu karesna redes womasve finul is right: subject man = manu; object car = kare + -s + -na (object); red takes e from kare, plus -s; then the owner: woman = woma + -s + -ve (owner); verb fin + -ul (future), last. manu karena redes womasve finul puts -s on the adjective but not on the noun. manu karesna redes womasve finar uses the present ending -ar. manuna kares redes womasve finul puts -na on the subject instead of the object.
